Subject: Private VPC: edge demarcation sketch and questions

Hi Soojin / Irene,

Thanks for the sync yesterday. Attached is the initial sketch of our proposed demarcation (see 20260527-avantedge-vpc-sketch-v1.pdf). A few constraints from our side:
- Only management plane (SSH/HTTPS) allowed from the operations subnet via a hardened bastion (no direct inbound).
- Egress to public endpoints must go through a customer-managed NAT; we cannot accept direct outbound from the data plane.
- We have BGP to the on-prem WAN but would prefer static routes for the initial cutover.

Two clarifying questions:
1) What specific control-plane endpoints from Redwood must be reachable (FQDNs/IP ranges + ports)?
2) For the operator handback, what evidence do you require to consider the deployment "operationally handed back" to our SREs?

We want to avoid surprises during the weekend cutover.

Regards,
Carlos Mendez
Senior Solutions Architect
AvantEdge Systems

Carlos — thanks for the sketch, that helps. High level answers up front and a short ask: please confirm the bastion's egress SNAT IP(s) and the maintenance window for the cutover.

Short answers:
- Control-plane endpoints: our control plane requires outbound HTTPS (443) to a small set of hostnames that we publish per-deployment (we'll provide exact FQDNs and short-lived IP lists). We also use a mutual mTLS tunnel from the control-plane agent on the cluster to Redwood's control plane for telemetry/health checks (egress ports 443 + ephemeral TLS ports).
- Operator handback: we typically ask for (a) successful canary traffic for 24 hours, (b) completed runbook execution and alarm thresholds validated, (c) access to audit logs + network ACLs, and (d) a security checklist signed by the customer's infra lead.

I'm attaching a draft operator-handback checklist (20260527-operator-handback-checklist-draft.md) — this is our starting point. Aditya, can you list the minimal network rules we need so Carlos can validate with their firewall team?

Thanks,

Looping in technical notes — quoted for thread continuity.

On Wed, May 27, 2026 at 10:03 AM soojin_lee@redwood.com wrote:
> I'm attaching a draft operator-handback checklist ... Aditya, can you list the minimal network rules we need so Carlos can validate with their firewall team?

Notes / recommendations (minimal):
- Control-plane egress: TCP 443 to these FQDNs (we will publish): cp-*.redwood-inference.net (short-lived IPs; allow hostname-based egress or weekly CIDR update).
- mTLS: outbound from control-agent to cp-mtls.redwood-inference.net:443. Must support TLS SNI and client certs (we provision certs during onboarding).
- Health/telemetry: UDP 123 (NTP) to the customer's clock pool OR permit outbound NTP to our NTP endpoint if they prefer centralized time; time sync is required for cert validation.
- DNS: outbound UDP/TCP 53 to their resolver (we don't require public DNS egress if resolver is able to resolve cp hostnames).
- Ephemeral ports: permit ephemeral outbound 1024-65535 for agent-initiated connections; NAT will be fine as long as SNAT mapping is stable for the session (we use long-lived sessions for some agents).
- Data-plane: must not egress directly to public internet. Any model telemetry or logs that need upload should be routed to the NAT with explicit allowlist to cp hostnames.
- Recommended: an allowlist of the bastion SNAT IP(s) so we can correlate logs and allow admin access from there.

Operational guidance:
- If AvantEdge prefers static routing, advertise the route to the customer WAN and configure a firewall policy that permits only the listed FQDNs/IPs.
- We can provide a script that validates connectivity to all required endpoints and produces a report for the handback checklist.

Action: Carlos — can you confirm bastion SNAT IP(s) and whether your infra team can accept host-based FQDN egress rules vs. CIDR lists?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Network Lead, Deployment Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Carlos Mendez <carlos@avantedge.com>

Thanks Aditya — this is exactly the level of detail our firewall team needs. Quick answers:
- Bastion SNAT IPs: 3.34.122.19 and 3.34.122.20 (these are static elastic IPs we will use for outbound admin/NAT).
- We cannot do hostname-only allowlists at the firewall layer; we need CIDR/IPv4 ranges. We'll accept a weekly IP range export from Redwood during the onboarding window.
- NTP: we'll allow UDP 123 to our internal stratum pool.
- Ephemeral ports: OK behind NAT.

I've attached our firewall rules export (20260527-firewall-export.csv) showing how we propose to map your required hosts to our CIDR exceptions for the cutover weekend. We can do the weekend maintenance window: Saturday 2026-06-05 00:00–04:00 PT.

Two small asks from our side before we sign off on handback:
1) A small run of the connectivity-validation script against our bastion SNATs to prove control-plane reachability.
2) A short SOW amendment clarifying the responsibilities for log retention and audit access post-handoff.

Carlos
